helpHint.message: Getting started, features, and common questions.

helpIntro.message: Key workflows, shortcuts, and boundaries in zing.

helpStartBody.message: Click the zing toolbar icon or press the launch shortcut to open the palette (current: $1). Change the shortcut in Settings → Keyboard, or right-click the toolbar icon to edit the binding or open this guide in a new tab.

helpSearchBody.message: The empty home shows up to 10 suggested pages and commands based on successful use in zing, with curated commands when there is little history. Recommendations keep their order until the next opening. Search tabs, bookmarks, commands, and settings in one place using English or Chinese keywords, without mode prefixes. Combine page titles, domains, tab groups, or bookmark folders in any order—for example, “new tab”, “reopen last tab”, “theme”, or “downloads”. Browsing history from the past week joins search results. Search All History appears seventh, or at the end of shorter lists, to search all time. A slow history query does not block other results; late replies do not insert rows. Successfully opened history results share preferences with tabs at the same website address. Main search and Search All History apply habits only within the same relevance tier for the same query, show a history icon for remembered preferences. Hover or focus the icon to see why and what will be forgotten; click it to forget. You can also press Shift+Backspace on the selected result. Forgetting affects both history and tab results.

helpControlsBody.message: Right-click a result, click Actions in the footer, or press Cmd/Ctrl+K to open actions for the selected item. Lists also support Ctrl+P and Ctrl+N alongside the arrow keys.

helpBackBody.message: Press Esc, click the back arrow, or press Backspace in an empty secondary search field to go back one level with your search and selection restored. At the main search, Esc closes zing.

helpTabsBody.message: Pin, mute, and close actions apply directly to the selected result and keep the palette open for continuous cleanup; bulk close preserves pinned tabs. Search a tab group’s name to manage its tabs. Choose Zing: Tab Switcher to filter recent tabs inside the palette, then click a row or press Enter to switch; Cancel returns to your search. When launching the switcher with its shortcut, hold the modifier key to select and release to switch; click the search field or press Cmd/Ctrl+F to pause release-to-switch and filter by text instead.

helpTuckBody.message: “Tuck Away Tab” moves a tab into a collapsed group at the end of the window without closing or discarding it; switch to the tab from search anytime to bring it back. Enable “Auto Tuck Tabs” in Settings to automatically tuck tabs unused for 7 days. If a group needs confirmation after a browser restart, search for “recover tucked tabs”.

helpStorageBody.message: Search for “local storage”, “session storage”, or “cookies” on a webpage. Select a key on the left to preview its value on the right; Enter or Copy Value copies the original string. JSON is formatted for reading; storage is read-only. Reading cookies requests permission only for the current site’s domains, which you can revoke anytime in Chrome’s extension settings.

helpShortcutBody.message: If a shortcut is unassigned or conflicts, open Settings → Keyboard to change it in Chrome’s extension shortcuts page. Due to browser limits, Ctrl+Tab requires one-time manual setup—search for “ctrl tab” for the setup code and steps.

helpWindowBody.message: zing opens as an in-page overlay on ordinary webpages, and automatically falls back to a separate panel or toolbar popup on Chrome internal pages, restricted sites, or when the address bar has focus.

helpPrivacyBody.message: zing has no account, server, or telemetry. Preferences and learned search ranking stay on your device; website storage values stay only in the current panel’s memory. Browsing history requires the history permission at installation. zing keeps no persistent copy of the history database; it remembers only search terms and website addresses you explicitly select and successfully open. Reading history or a failed open creates no learning record. Incognito windows do not read ordinary history or record selections.
